articles.excerpt: New Google AdMob AI tools help app developers fix setups fast, protect brand safety, and automate monetization in code.

We are introducing new AI tools in AdMob to help you manage your app business with less manual effort. You can now use a conversational assistant to fix technical errors, find new revenue opportunities, and set brand safety rules using simple language. We are also providing tools that allow your AI agents to write and validate ad code directly. You remain in control by reviewing and approving every change before it goes live. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Building a successful mobile app means balancing a great user experience with ads monetization. But manually managing ad setups, fixing integration errors, and auditing brand safety pulls your team’s focus away from building. To help you simplify operations and accelerate your productivity, we’re introducing new AI tools for AdMob, Ask AdMob, agent skills and an MCP server. These new tools, built with Google AI, can help you earn more revenue and build your app business faster. Fine-tune your monetization with Ask AdMob Ask AdMob, a conversational agent built with Gemini, will live directly in your AdMob account. Trained on AdMob monetization best practices, it can help fix issues, find revenue opportunities, and protect your brand safety like an AdMob product expert. Here are a few examples of what Ask AdMob can do for you. Find and fix setup issues, skipping the manual guesswork: The troubleshooting hub will help you spot setup anomalies and SDK integration issues. Ask AdMob has visibility into how ads are loading in your app so it can highlight recommendations to resolve issues impacting your revenue. Identify new revenue opportunities: Ask AdMob uses peer benchmarks to recommend high-value SDK bidders with predicted revenue uplifts to add to your setup and help optimize your mediation groups. For example, Ask AdMob will automatically check your third-party network configuration to catch costly typos and floor price discrepancies before they impact your yield. Create effective brand safety rules with natural language: Instead of manually managing blocklists, you can configure custom brand safety rules using simple, natural-language prompts in your AdMob UI. We’ll begin testing these capabilities over the next few months and continue evolving Ask AdMob with more advanced features to take action on your behalf later next year. As always, you remain in control, reviewing and approving every recommendation before it’s applied. Manage ad setups directly with your AI agent Previously, setting up ad placements meant clicking through web dashboards, copying and pasting ad unit IDs, and managing ad configuration files outside your codebase. With AdMob agent skills and an upcoming MCP server, we’re giving you the tools to enable your preferred AI agent to build, edit, and validate ad code for your app. AdMob agent skills give your AI agent pre-built, tested playbooks to implement coding tasks like, migrating to the Google Mobile Ads Next-Gen SDK, validating your SDK implementation, and implementing new ad formats in your app. Find these skills and more on our developer site . While agent skills can help you implement tasks today, we’re also working on an AdMob MCP server to connect your developer environments directly with AdMob. Soon your AI agent will be able to read account data, write new ad units, and manage mediation settings. All you have to do is review and approve the updates before you push them to production. This is in early testing and will be expanding to more developers early next year. Prepare your business for a more agentic 2027 Throughout 2027, we’ll introduce a much broader and more advanced wave of AI tools for app developers — expanding both in-product and AI agent capabilities. These tools will handle more of the routine operational workload so you can focus on what matters most: your product, your users, and your business. articles.title: An Update on the Content We Recommend on Instagram in India
articles.excerpt: We've strengthened the default protections behind what Instagram recommends in India to reduce unwanted content and improve people’s experience on Instagram. This work has been guided by what our users told us they want from their recommendations. The post An Update on the Content We Recommend on Instagram in India appeared first on Meta Newsroom .

This work has been guided by what our users told us they want from their recommendations. Today, we’re sharing an update on this work. How Recommendations Work At Instagram, we make personalized recommendations to help people discover new communities and content. Our goal is to make recommendations that are relevant and valuable to each person who sees them. For example, if you interact with restaurants and bookstores on Instagram, we may recommend content about food, recipes, books, or reading. Recommendations include content from accounts you don’t already follow, in places like Explore, Reels and Feed , so we apply guidelines specific to them. Through our Recommendations Guidelines , we work to avoid recommending content that could be low quality, objectionable or particularly sensitive. We use technology to detect content and accounts that don’t meet those guidelines and to help us avoid recommending them. As always, content that goes against our Community Standards is removed from Instagram, and content that is unlawful in a country is restricted there. What We’ve Changed Better detection: Around the world, our systems check content against our Recommendations Guidelines before we recommend it. We’ve been improving those systems, including using more capable AI models that assess content directly rather than waiting for someone to report or hide it, so we catch more of what people don’t want to see. Tuned for India: We’ve improved our systems specifically for India so they catch more of what people here told us they didn’t want to see. Today, our systems keep more of this content out of recommendations, including sexually suggestive content and content that depicts violence. Since these changes, we’ve been able to proactively reduce more content in India that doesn’t meet our Recommendations Guidelines. As a result, we’ve seen people report recommended content about half as often as they were a year ago. Your feedback shapes this too. When someone hides a post or taps “Not interested,” that tells us what not to recommend to them, and helps us understand what people don’t want to see. Controls Over What You See and Who Can Reach You Alongside the standards we apply for everyone, you have controls to adjust what you see and who can reach you: Sensitive Content Control lets people choose to see less sensitive content in their recommendations, across Search, Reels, Explore, suggested accounts, and in-Feed recommendations. It’s in Settings and Activity, under Content Preferences. In India, the most mature content isn’t recommended, so this control adjusts what you see within that. Political Content Control lets people choose to see less political content in recommendations from accounts they don’t follow. It’s in Settings and Activity, under Content Preferences → Political Content. Not Interested lets people tell us a recommendation isn’t for them, by tapping the three dots on a post or reel. Hidden Words filters chosen words, phrases, and emojis out of comments and message requests. Block prevents someone from finding a profile, seeing posts, or sending messages, and also covers new accounts they try to create. Teens have additional age appropriate protections. Last year, we introduced Teen Accounts in India, which automatically places teens in a 13+ content setting shaped by our age-appropriate content guidelines . Our Continued Work We’re committed to improving our systems as user behavior and technology changes, and we’ll keep listening to what people in India tell us they want to see. We publish data on how we enforce our policies in our global Community Standards Enforcement Report , and in the monthly transparency report we publish for India under the IT Rules, 2021.
